title: Kennedy, Three Globalizations of Law and Legal Thought 1850–2000

1.title: What the article does and what its three periods are
1.text: DUNCAN KENNEDY, 'THREE GLOBALIZATIONS OF LAW AND LEGAL THOUGHT: 1850–2000'. The study of 'law and development' began with a particular positioning of the two terms: it asked HOW LEGAL REFORM COULD CONTRIBUTE TO THE TAKE-OFF INTO SELF-SUSTAINING GROWTH in the post-colonial Third World of the 1960s. TRUBEK AND GALANTER ('Scholars in Self-Estrangement', 1974) reconstructed those terms: they problematised the rather simple instrumental conception of law and POLITICISED our understanding of development. Kennedy's three globalizations refer to TWO OVERLAPPING PERIODS of legal institutional and conceptual change in the West: the rise of CLASSICAL LEGAL THOUGHT (CLT) BETWEEN 1850 AND 1914 and of SOCIALLY ORIENTED LEGAL THOUGHT BETWEEN 1900 AND 1968 — and to the transformation of the characteristic features of both periods IN TWO DISTINCT PROCESSES OF DIFFUSION across the world of colonies and newly independent nation states. A shorter third part sketches a similar development FOR THE PERIOD 1945–2000. And at once a warning fundamental to the method: FRAME AND CONTEXT ARE MISLEADING TERMS for the relation of legal and economic activity, because ECONOMIC ACTIVITY CANNOT BE UNDERSTOOD AS SOMETHING AUTONOMOUS in relation to a set of passive institutional and conceptual constraints. LEGAL INSTITUTIONS AND IDEAS STAND IN A DYNAMIC, DIALECTICAL OR CONSTITUTIVE RELATION TO ECONOMIC ACTIVITY.

cards.q: Which three globalizations does Kennedy distinguish, and in which years?
cards.a: 1) CLASSICAL LEGAL THOUGHT (CLT) 1850–1914. 2) SOCIALLY ORIENTED LEGAL THOUGHT ('the social') 1900–1968. 3) POLICY ANALYSIS, NEOFORMALISM AND ADJUDICATION 1945–2000. The first two are periods of change in the West PLUS their diffusion into the colonies and newly independent states.

cards.q: Why does Kennedy refuse to speak of law as the 'frame' or 'context' of the economy?
cards.a: Because ECONOMIC ACTIVITY CANNOT BE UNDERSTOOD AS SOMETHING AUTONOMOUS in relation to a set of passive institutional and conceptual constraints, as those terms suggest. LEGAL INSTITUTIONS AND IDEAS STAND IN A DYNAMIC, DIALECTICAL OR CONSTITUTIVE RELATION TO ECONOMIC ACTIVITY.

2.title: Who makes law: not only policy-makers
2.text: The changing 'frame' was also A PLAN, a project of those with access to the legislative, administrative and judicial processes of colonies and states — a project of influencing economic activity. SINCE THE MID-18TH CENTURY (the French PHYSIOCRATS), at least sometimes one of the objects of legislation, administration and adjudication was ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT as it was then understood. THE FIRST GLOBALIZATION CAN BE SEEN AS THE CULMINATION OF THE LIBERAL ATTACK ON MERCANTILIST OR 'EARLY MODERN' ECONOMIC AND SOCIAL POLICY, AND THE SECOND AS THE POLITICAL PROGRAMME OF THE FIRST GENERATION OF CRITICS OF THE FRUITS OF LAISSEZ-FAIRE. But the frame is not merely the plan of 'policy-makers': in the capitalist West and on its periphery alike, POWERFUL ECONOMIC ACTORS INFLUENCE THE MAKING OF LAW JUST AS THEY ARE CONSTRAINED BY IT. The transition from mercantilism to liberalism was as much or more their work as that of statesmen and thinkers. AND THE RISE OF 'THE SOCIAL' WAS A FUNCTION OF THE RISE OF POLITICAL PARTIES AGGREGATING THE INTERESTS OF WEAK ECONOMIC ACTORS, ESPECIALLY FARMERS AND WORKERS, IN REACTION TO THE INFLUENCE OF CAPITAL. In the struggles over regimes, what is at stake are the institutional and conceptual possibilities of law, the repertoire of possible policies and great numbers of concrete rules; and actors with privileged access to the legal apparatus — the advocates of economic actors, lawyers as legislators, judges and academics — have a PROFESSIONALLY LEGITIMATED ROLE that is bound up, in parallel and overlapping ways, with the role of the holders of economic power.

cards.q: How does Kennedy define the first and second globalizations in terms of economic policy?
cards.a: THE FIRST is THE CULMINATION OF THE LIBERAL ATTACK ON MERCANTILIST ('early modern') economic and social policy. THE SECOND is THE POLITICAL PROGRAMME OF THE FIRST GENERATION OF CRITICS OF THE FRUITS OF LAISSEZ-FAIRE.

cards.q: What, on Kennedy's account, was the rise of 'the social' a function of?
cards.a: OF THE RISE OF POLITICAL PARTIES AGGREGATING THE INTERESTS OF WEAK ECONOMIC ACTORS — especially FARMERS AND WORKERS — IN REACTION TO THE INFLUENCE OF CAPITAL. It is therefore not merely the work of thinkers: powerful economic actors influence the making of law just as they are constrained by it.

3.title: What was globalized and by what — three mechanisms
3.text: BETWEEN 1850 AND 1914 CLASSICAL LEGAL THOUGHT (CLT) was globalized. IT HAD NO ESSENCE, but among its important features was that it was A WAY OF THINKING ABOUT LAW AS A SYSTEM OF SPHERES OF AUTONOMY FOR PRIVATE AND PUBLIC ACTORS, THE BOUNDARIES OF THE SPHERES BEING DETERMINED BY LEGAL REASONING UNDERSTOOD AS A SCIENTIFIC PRACTICE. The mechanisms of that globalization: DIRECT WESTERN IMPOSITION in the colonised world, the FORCED 'OPENING' of non-Western regimes that remained independent, and THE PRESTIGE OF GERMAN LEGAL SCIENCE in the world of European and Western nation states. BETWEEN 1900 AND 1968 'THE SOCIAL' was globalized — again a mode of thought without an essence, but with an important feature: A PREOCCUPATION WITH THINKING OF LAW AS A PURPOSIVE ACTIVITY, AS A REGULATORY MECHANISM THAT CAN AND OUGHT TO FACILITATE THE EVOLUTION OF SOCIAL LIFE IN ACCORDANCE WITH AN EVER-INCREASING PERCEIVED SOCIAL INTERDEPENDENCE AT EVERY LEVEL, FROM THE FAMILY TO THE WORLD OF NATIONS. The agents of diffusion were REFORM MOVEMENTS OF EVERY POLITICAL STRIPE in the developed West, NATIONALIST MOVEMENTS on the periphery, and the ELITES OF THE NEWLY INDEPENDENT STATES after 1945. BETWEEN 1945 AND 2000 one tendency was to think legal technique, after the critiques of CLT and of the social alike, as THE PRAGMATIC BALANCING OF CONFLICTING CONSIDERATIONS in administering the system created by the social jurists; at the same time there was a seemingly contrary tendency to see law as THE GUARANTOR OF HUMAN AND PROPERTY RIGHTS AND OF THE INTERGOVERNMENTAL ORDER through the gradual extension of the rule of law understood as JUDICIAL SUPREMACY. The mechanisms: THE AMERICAN VICTORY IN THE SECOND WORLD WAR AND THE COLD WAR, the 'OPENING' of nation states to a new legal consciousness through participation in the world market on the terms of transnational corporations and international regulatory institutions, and THE PRESTIGE OF AMERICAN CULTURE.

cards.q: What was the 'way of thinking' in CLT that was globalized?
cards.a: Thinking of law AS A SYSTEM OF SPHERES OF AUTONOMY FOR PRIVATE AND PUBLIC ACTORS, THE BOUNDARIES OF THOSE SPHERES BEING DETERMINED BY LEGAL REASONING UNDERSTOOD AS A SCIENTIFIC PRACTICE. CLT itself, on Kennedy's account, HAD NO ESSENCE.

cards.q: Name the mechanisms of diffusion for all three globalizations.
cards.a: FIRST: direct Western imposition in the colonies, the forced 'OPENING' of independent non-Western regimes, THE PRESTIGE OF GERMAN LEGAL SCIENCE. SECOND: reform movements of every political stripe in the West, NATIONALIST MOVEMENTS on the periphery, the elites of newly independent states after 1945. THIRD: the American victory in the Second World War and the Cold War, the 'opening' of states through the world market, THE PRESTIGE OF AMERICAN CULTURE.

cards.q: What was the chief preoccupation of 'the social'?
cards.a: TO THINK OF LAW AS A PURPOSIVE ACTIVITY, AS A REGULATORY MECHANISM THAT CAN AND OUGHT TO FACILITATE THE EVOLUTION OF SOCIAL LIFE IN ACCORDANCE WITH AN EVER-INCREASING PERCEIVED SOCIAL INTERDEPENDENCE AT EVERY LEVEL — FROM THE FAMILY TO THE WORLD OF NATIONS.

4.title: What was NOT globalized — and why that matters
4.text: The 'thing' that was globalized WAS IN NONE OF THOSE THREE PERIODS THE VIEW OF LAW OF ANY PARTICULAR POLITICAL IDEOLOGY. CLASSICAL LEGAL THOUGHT WAS LIBERAL EITHER CONSERVATIVELY OR PROGRESSIVELY, depending on how it balanced the public and the private in the market and in the household. THE SOCIAL COULD BE SOCIALIST, SOCIAL DEMOCRATIC, CATHOLIC OR SOCIAL CHRISTIAN, OR FASCIST — BUT NOT COMMUNIST OR CLASSICALLY LIBERAL. Modern legal consciousness is THE COMMON PROPERTY OF RIGHT-WING AND LEFT-WING RIGHTS THEORISTS AND OF RIGHT-WING AND LEFT-WING POLICY ANALYSTS. Nor was it a philosophy of law in the usual sense: in each period, positivism and natural law, various theories of rights and in time varieties of pragmatism all sat comfortably under the same big tent within that mode of thought. AND WHAT WAS CERTAINLY NOT GLOBALIZED WAS ANY PARTICULAR BODY OF LEGAL RULES: EACH MODE PROVIDED THE MATERIAL FROM WHICH JURISTS AND LEGISLATORS COULD MANUFACTURE AN INFINITE VARIETY OF PARTICULAR POSITIVE LAWS — and manufacture it they did, even while claiming merely to transplant rules from one setting to another.

cards.q: Which political ideologies fitted inside CLT and inside the social?
cards.a: CLT was LIBERAL either CONSERVATIVELY or PROGRESSIVELY. THE SOCIAL could be SOCIALIST, SOCIAL DEMOCRATIC, CATHOLIC OR SOCIAL CHRISTIAN, OR FASCIST — BUT NOT COMMUNIST OR CLASSICALLY LIBERAL. Modern consciousness is the common property of right and left alike.

cards.q: Was any particular body of legal rules globalized?
cards.a: CERTAINLY NOT. Each mode provided only THE MATERIAL from which jurists and legislators manufactured AN INFINITE VARIETY OF PARTICULAR POSITIVE LAWS — and they did so even when claiming merely to transplant rules from one setting to another.

5.title: Langue and parole — the key to the whole article
5.text: Kennedy uses the Saussurean pair, and without it the article cannot be read. CONSCIOUSNESS, UNDERSTOOD AS A VOCABULARY OF CONCEPTS AND TYPICAL ARGUMENTS, IS THE 'LANGUE' — THE LANGUAGE. THE PARTICULAR, POSITIVELY ENACTED RULES OF INDIVIDUAL COUNTRIES INTO WHICH THE LANGUE WAS GLOBALIZED ARE THE 'PAROLE' — SPEECH. Just as a particular sentence, say 'shut the door', is uttered in a particular language, a legal norm is a binding utterance in a particular legal discourse. And just as there is AN INFINITY of grammatically correct sentences that can be uttered in English, there is AN INFINITY of regulatory statutes that can be formulated in the conceptual vocabulary of the social and defended by an infinite variety of particular justifying arguments composed and recomposed from the political sound bites of the social. The elements of a mode of thought arose piecemeal in various civilian and common law countries, and Kennedy distinguishes TWO PROCESSES: (1) the emergence of a TRANSNATIONAL MODE OF THOUGHT as jurists combine ideas of various origins and displace the preceding transnational mode; (2) the GEOGRAPHICAL DIFFUSION of the transnational mode — either by the direct and complete replacement of an older legal regime by the new one, as in colonial expansion, or by 'RECEPTION' of the emerging mode, which combines with 'indigenous' elements and the residue of the previous mode into A NEW NATIONAL SYNTHESIS. Following DIEGO LOPEZ MEDINA one can identify sites of 'PRODUCTION' of the new transnational mode as against sites where there is mere reception with minimal dialectical feedback. IN THIS SENSE GERMAN LEGAL THOUGHT WAS HEGEMONIC BETWEEN 1850 AND 1900, FRENCH BETWEEN 1900 AND THE 1930s, AND AMERICAN AFTER 1950.

terms.def: Langue = the vocabulary of concepts and typical arguments (consciousness). Parole = the particular, positively enacted rules of individual countries.

cards.q: What do 'langue' and 'parole' mean in Kennedy?
cards.a: LANGUE = legal consciousness understood as A VOCABULARY OF CONCEPTS AND TYPICAL ARGUMENTS. PAROLE = THE PARTICULAR, POSITIVELY ENACTED RULES of individual countries. Just as there is an infinity of grammatically correct sentences, there is an infinity of statutes formulable in the vocabulary of the social — WHAT IS GLOBALIZED IS THE LANGUE, NOT THE PAROLE.

cards.q: Which legal thought was hegemonic in which period?
cards.a: GERMAN 1850–1900, FRENCH from 1900 into the 1930s, AMERICAN after 1950. A distinction is drawn between the site of PRODUCTION of a new transnational mode and the site of mere RECEPTION with minimal feedback (Diego Lopez Medina).

6.title: Four heterodox claims about American law
6.text: Kennedy's account dissents from the mainstream of American legal history in four respects. FIRST it portrays the USA UNTIL THE 1930s AS A CONTEXT OF LEGAL RECEPTION, that is AS PART OF THE PERIPHERY OR SEMI-PERIPHERY: legal development was strongly determined by what was happening in Germany and later in France, and THE ORIGINAL AMERICAN SYNTHESIS HAD NO INFLUENCE ON THOSE COUNTRIES. It thereby attacks the main tradition, which explains the transformations of American legal thought by internal social and economic development. SECOND it stresses HOW FAR DEVELOPMENTS IN DIFFERENT FIELDS OF LAW OVER THE LAST CENTURY HAVE FOLLOWED A SINGLE PATTERN: histories of individual fields constantly attribute to an internal dynamic changes that occurred in precisely parallel ways in other fields, and are therefore as unconvincing as national histories that disregard the transnational movement of legal thought. THIRD it departs from fashion by TREATING LEGAL REALISM AS THE CRITICAL DESTRUCTION OF SOCIOLOGICAL JURISPRUDENCE (that is, of 'the social'), NOT AS ITS 'ESSENTIAL' CONTINUATION. FOURTH, on his account the post-war developments are characterised AS MUCH BY THE NEOFORMALIST LEGAL CONSCIOUSNESS OF THE WARREN COURT AND OF THE NEOLIBERALS AS BY THE CONFLICTING-CONSIDERATIONS CONSCIOUSNESS OF THE LEGAL PROCESS SCHOOL — AND BOTH WERE RESPONSES TO THE DEMISE OF THE SOCIAL, NOT OF CLT.

cards.q: Why does Kennedy place the USA on the periphery until the 1930s?
cards.a: Because its legal development was STRONGLY DETERMINED by what was happening in GERMANY and later in FRANCE, while THE ORIGINAL AMERICAN SYNTHESIS HAD NO INFLUENCE ON THOSE COUNTRIES. He thereby attacks the tradition that explains American legal change by internal social and economic development.

cards.q: How does Kennedy assess legal realism, and what were the post-war movements a response to?
cards.a: He treats legal realism as THE CRITICAL DESTRUCTION OF SOCIOLOGICAL JURISPRUDENCE (the social), NOT as its continuation. And the post-war developments — the neoformalism of the Warren Court and of the neoliberals, and the conflicting considerations of the Legal Process school — WERE RESPONSES TO THE DEMISE OF THE SOCIAL, NOT OF CLT.

7.title: CLT: three features and the will theory
7.text: THE FIRST GLOBALIZATION took place in the second half of the 19th century and ENDED WITH THE FIRST WORLD WAR. On the account of its social critics and of most present-day historians alike, the mainstream of the late 19th century saw law as a 'SYSTEM' with a strong internal structural coherence resting on THREE FEATURES: (1) THE EXHAUSTIVE ELABORATION OF THE DISTINCTION BETWEEN PRIVATE AND PUBLIC LAW, (2) 'INDIVIDUALISM' and (3) A COMMITMENT TO LEGAL INTERPRETIVE FORMALISM. Those three features came together in the 'WILL THEORY'. THE WILL THEORY HELD THAT THE PRIVATE LAW RULES OF THE 'ADVANCED' WESTERN NATION STATES CAN BE WELL UNDERSTOOD AS A SET OF RATIONAL DERIVATIONS FROM THE IDEA THAT GOVERNMENT SHOULD PROTECT THE RIGHTS OF LEGAL PERSONS, THAT IS, HELP THEM TO REALISE THEIR WILLS, RESTRICTED ONLY IN SO FAR AS IS NECESSARY TO ALLOW OTHERS TO DO THE SAME. It was an attempt to identify the rules that follow from a consensus in favour of the goal of individual self-realisation. IT WAS NOT A POLITICAL OR MORAL PHILOSOPHY justifying that goal; nor a positive historical or sociological theory of how it became the goal. IT WAS A SPECIFIC, WILL-BASED AND DEDUCTIVE ACCOUNT OF THE INTERRELATION OF DOZENS OR HUNDREDS OF RELATIVELY CONCRETE NORMS of existing national legal orders and of the institutions that made and applied them.

terms.def: Private law rules are rational derivations from the idea that government should protect the rights of persons, that is help them realise their wills, restricted only so far as to allow others to do the same.

cards.q: On which three features does the coherence of CLT rest?
cards.a: 1) THE EXHAUSTIVE ELABORATION OF THE DISTINCTION BETWEEN PRIVATE AND PUBLIC LAW. 2) 'INDIVIDUALISM'. 3) A COMMITMENT TO LEGAL INTERPRETIVE FORMALISM. The three come together in the WILL THEORY.

cards.q: How does the will theory run, and what is it not?
cards.a: The private law rules of advanced states are A SET OF RATIONAL DERIVATIONS FROM THE IDEA THAT GOVERNMENT SHOULD PROTECT THE RIGHTS OF LEGAL PERSONS, that is help them REALISE THEIR WILLS, restricted only so far as to allow others to do the same. It is NOT a political or moral philosophy justifying that goal, nor a historical or sociological theory of its emergence — it is AN ACCOUNT OF THE INTERRELATION OF CONCRETE NORMS.

8.title: The German historical school, the pandectists and Savigny
8.text: 'Outside' or 'above' legal theory there were more justifications for the commitment to individualism, but ONLY NATURAL RIGHTS THEORY WAS HIGHLY RELEVANT 'INSIDE' AS WELL, that is in the development of a technique of legal analysis based on deduction: from the 17th century the natural rights theorists elaborated the will theory as a set of implications from their normative premises, AND THEIR PARTICULAR LEGAL TECHNIQUE WAS THE DIRECT ANCESTOR OF THE LEGAL FORMALISM THE SOCIAL REFORMERS ATTACKED IN ITS POSITIVISED FORM. In the 19th century the GERMAN HISTORICAL SCHOOL developed A POSITIVIST VERSION OF NORMATIVE FORMALISM: the national system of law in fact reflects the normative order of the underlying society; that order is coherent, or tends towards coherence, on the basis of the SPIRIT AND HISTORY of the people in question; and 'legal scientists' can and should elaborate the positive rules constituting the 'system' on the premise of its INTERNAL COHERENCE. The German PANDECTISTS (WINDSCHEID, for example) worked with the analysis of the fundamental concepts of the German common-law version of Roman law — RIGHT, WILL, FAULT, PERSON — with the aim of showing that the system could be made INTERNALLY COHERENT and brought closer to GAPLESSNESS. MANY CONTINENTAL LEGAL SCIENTISTS UNDERSTOOD THE GERMAN CIVIL CODE OF 1900 AS THE LEGISLATIVE ADOPTION OF THIS SYSTEM.

cards.q: What did the German historical school do with formalism?
cards.a: It developed A POSITIVIST VERSION of it: the national system of law in fact reflects the normative order of society; that order is coherent on the basis of the SPIRIT AND HISTORY of the people concerned; and 'legal scientists' should elaborate the positive rules on the premise of the system's INTERNAL COHERENCE.

cards.q: What fundamental concepts did the pandectists work with, and how does that relate to the BGB?
cards.a: With RIGHT, WILL, FAULT AND PERSON in the German common-law version of Roman law; the aim was to show that the system could be made INTERNALLY COHERENT and brought closer to GAPLESSNESS. Many continental scientists understood THE GERMAN CIVIL CODE OF 1900 as THE LEGISLATIVE ADOPTION OF THAT SYSTEM.

9.title: Savigny's paradox and the hero of the first globalization
9.text: THE HEROIC FIGURE OF THE FIRST GLOBALIZATION WAS THE PROFESSOR OF LAW — the author of codes, of their statutory amendments and of the textbooks — and the great inspiring predecessor was the founder of the historical school FRIEDRICH CARL VON SAVIGNY (1779–1861). And here is the paradox that is the likely source of his fundamental importance: IN THE SINGLE IDEA OF LEGAL SCIENCE AS THE ELABORATION OF A 'SYSTEM', SAVIGNY COMBINED THE UNIVERSALISING, LEGAL-FORMALIST WILL THEORY WITH THE IDEA THAT PARTICULAR REGIMES OF STATE LAW REFLECT DIVERSE UNDERLYING EXTRA-LEGAL SOCIAL NORMATIVE ORDERS. His approach sharply attacked the notion that all national legal regimes are merely better or worse approximations to a religiously or rationally founded transnational natural law. OUTSIDE GERMANY the historical school was a MINORITY TENDENCY, but the same conception of the will theory, joining individualism to deductive form, gradually displaced older ways of understanding private law. AUSTIN was a follower of the Germans, and his LECTURES ON JURISPRUDENCE, written in 1831–2 but published only in 1863, were THE MANIFESTO OF CLT FOR THE COMMON LAW WORLD. The normative or 'external' force for that theory might come from UTILITARIANISM, from Lockean, Kantian or French revolutionary NATURAL RIGHTS, or from a variety of EVOLUTIONISM (the movement of progressive societies was from contract to status; social Darwinism). But wherever it was derived from, NORMATIVE INDIVIDUALISM WAS TIGHTLY BOUND UP WITH THE LOGICAL METHOD IN CONSTRUCTING SOME VERSION OF THE WILL THEORY.

cards.q: What is Savigny's paradox?
cards.a: That IN A SINGLE IDEA of legal science as the elaboration of a 'system' he COMBINED THE UNIVERSALISING, LEGAL-FORMALIST WILL THEORY WITH THE IDEA THAT PARTICULAR REGIMES OF STATE LAW REFLECT DIVERSE UNDERLYING EXTRA-LEGAL NORMATIVE ORDERS. That is the likely source of his fundamental importance.

cards.q: Who was the heroic figure of the first globalization, and what was the manifesto of CLT for the common law?
cards.a: THE PROFESSOR OF LAW — author of codes, of their statutory amendments and of the textbooks. The manifesto of CLT for the common law world was AUSTIN'S 'LECTURES ON JURISPRUDENCE', written in 1831–2 but published only in 1863; Austin was a follower of the Germans.

10.title: Why both left and right fitted inside CLT
10.text: The will theory served several purposes in legal discourse: it guided the scientific reconceptualisation, reorganisation and reform of private law rules in what the participants understood as AN APOLITICAL RATIONALISING PROJECT. But IT ALSO PROVIDED THE DISCURSIVE FRAME FOR THE DECISION OF HUNDREDS OR THOUSANDS OF CASES across the industrialising West IN WHICH LABOUR CLASHED WITH CAPITAL AND SMALL BUSINESS WITH LARGE. And it supplied an abstract, overarching ideological formulation of the meaning of the rule of law as an essential component of a liberal legal order. LEFT-WING AND RIGHT-WING POLITICAL PROJECTS COULD COEXIST WITHIN CLASSICAL LEGAL THOUGHT IN ITS HEYDAY BECAUSE THE 'WILL THEORY' WAS, FOR ALL ITS CLAIMS TO SCIENTIFICITY, HIGHLY MANIPULABLE AS TO WHAT EXACTLY FALLS WITHIN THE CATEGORIES OF RIGHT AND WILL — not to mention the ambiguities of the concept of legal personality as applied to private corporations and trade unions. CLT FIRMLY EXCLUDED ONLY HIERARCHICAL ORGANICISM IN THE MODE OF MONARCHISM OR NEO-FEUDALISM (DeMAISTRE) AND LEFT COLLECTIVISM IN THE MODE OF COMMUNISM OR UTOPIAN SOCIALISM (FOURIER). A minority current within CLT, but the mainstream of lay left thinking in the late 19th and early 20th century, were two ideas: THAT THE LEGAL ORDER PROVIDES INADEQUATE PROTECTION FOR 'WORKERS' RIGHTS' AND THAT CONTRACTS UNDER CAPITALISM DO NOT REPRESENT 'FREE WILL'. For all Marx's thundering against it, the populist idea that the problem lies in the skewing of the rules against the masses and in favour of 'the interests' never let go and was available to feminists and anti-colonialists before 1914. WHILE PROGRESSIVE REFORMERS IN THE PERIOD OF THE SOCIAL GENERALLY ABANDONED THE RHETORIC OF RIGHTS, AFTER THE SECOND WORLD WAR THEY REVIVED IT IN TWO FORMS: CIVIL LIBERTARIANISM AND THE IDEOLOGY OF INTERNATIONAL HUMAN RIGHTS.

cards.q: Why could left-wing and right-wing projects coexist within CLT?
cards.a: Because THE WILL THEORY WAS, FOR ALL ITS CLAIMS TO SCIENTIFICITY, HIGHLY MANIPULABLE as to what exactly falls within the categories of RIGHT and WILL (and what legal personality is — corporations, trade unions). CLT firmly excluded only HIERARCHICAL ORGANICISM (DeMaistre) and LEFT COLLECTIVISM (Fourier).

cards.q: What happened to the rhetoric of rights between CLT and the post-war period?
cards.a: A minority current of CLT held that the legal order inadequately protects 'workers' rights' and that contracts under capitalism are not 'free will'. PROGRESSIVE REFORMERS ABANDONED THE RHETORIC OF RIGHTS IN THE PERIOD OF THE SOCIAL — and AFTER THE SECOND WORLD WAR REVIVED IT in two forms: CIVIL LIBERTARIANISM and THE IDEOLOGY OF INTERNATIONAL HUMAN RIGHTS.

cards.q: How did CLT change over the course of the 20th century?
cards.a: Most of the juristic elite that developed and diffused it was CONSERVATIVE, and the main ideas of the first globalization changed during the 20th century FROM A 'CONSCIOUSNESS', within which a multitude of political projects was possible, INTO AN 'IDEOLOGY' — classical liberalism and then NEOLIBERALISM, one of the two central politico-theoretical projects of the modern right (the other being 'tradition').

11.title: How CLT spread: influence, imperialism and forced opening
11.text: The mechanism of the first globalization was A COMBINATION OF INFLUENCE WITHIN THE SYSTEM OF AUTONOMOUS WESTERN NATION STATES AND IMPERIALISM BROADLY CONCEIVED. THE GERMAN MODEL SPREAD NOT ONLY TO FRANCE BUT ACROSS EUROPE (western and eastern), ACROSS THE CHANNEL AND TO THE USA AND LATIN AMERICA. The USA and the British colonies, like Britain itself, ADOPTED GERMAN LEGAL SCIENCE AND ENORMOUS NUMBERS OF STATUTES BUT RESISTED CODIFICATION. The former Spanish colonies were more influenced by France and DID CODIFY. The English, French and Dutch, and later the Germans, Americans and Belgians, spread their national versions of CLT DIRECTLY INTO THEIR COLONIES, with codification or without (the Portuguese and Spanish doing the same in the remnants of their declining empires). THE GREAT POWERS FORCED AN 'OPENING' TO WESTERN LAW AS A COMPULSORY ASPECT OF THE OPENING TO WESTERN TRADE ON STATES THAT WERE NOT DIRECTLY COLONISED — ON THE OTTOMAN EMPIRE, JAPAN, CHINA, THAILAND, EGYPT AND IRAN. These sometimes adopted codes on European models and sometimes submitted to the establishment of SPECIAL COURTS APPLYING EUROPEAN LAW IN TRANSACTIONS WITH EUROPEANS. A subtler mode of CLT's globalization was implicit in the eventual universalisation of A SINGLE CLASSICAL SYSTEM OF PUBLIC INTERNATIONAL LAW, devised by the Western powers and founded on the conceptual innovations of the 17th-century natural lawyers: SOVEREIGNTY AS TERRITORIAL (NOT PERSONAL) POWER, ABSOLUTE WITHIN ITS SPHERE. In CLT the model of 'NATION STATE AND COLONY' was universal but for anachronisms, and THE HETEROGENEOUS MIX OF STRUCTURES OF GOVERNANCE OF THE WORLD OF 1800 WAS NOW ONLY A MEMORY. And finally there arose THE FIRST GLOBAL SYSTEM OF INTERNATIONAL ECONOMIC LAW founded on FREE TRADE, THE GOLD STANDARD AND PRIVATE INTERNATIONAL LAW (often applied by arbitrators): MONEY WAS DEPOLITICISED and an international capital market arose with its accompanying GUNBOAT DIPLOMACY.

cards.q: How exactly did CLT reach countries that were not colonised?
cards.a: THE GREAT POWERS FORCED AN 'OPENING' TO WESTERN LAW AS A COMPULSORY ASPECT OF THE OPENING TO WESTERN TRADE — on the OTTOMAN EMPIRE, JAPAN, CHINA, THAILAND, EGYPT AND IRAN. These either adopted codes on European models or submitted to SPECIAL COURTS APPLYING EUROPEAN LAW in transactions with Europeans.

cards.q: How did the reception of CLT differ in the Anglo-Saxon and the Latin American worlds?
cards.a: The USA, the British colonies and Britain ADOPTED GERMAN LEGAL SCIENCE AND ENORMOUS NUMBERS OF STATUTES BUT RESISTED CODIFICATION. The former Spanish colonies were more influenced by FRANCE and DID CODIFY.

cards.q: What did the first global system of international economic law rest on?
cards.a: On FREE TRADE, THE GOLD STANDARD AND PRIVATE INTERNATIONAL LAW (often applied by arbitrators). MONEY WAS DEPOLITICISED and an international capital market arose, with its accompanying GUNBOAT DIPLOMACY.

12.title: Why the peripheral elites accepted it — choice, not only imposition
12.text: Under direct colonisation there was at first no effective resistance to whatever the coloniser chose to impose. BUT IN WESTERN AND EASTERN EUROPE AND IN NORTH AND SOUTH AMERICA, CLT HAD FIRST TO WIN OVER THE ELITES OF INDEPENDENT NATION STATES. In the Ottoman lands and across Asia it was a matter of 'OPENING', not direct conquest, and there existed HIGHLY DEVELOPED PRIOR MODES OF LEGAL CONSCIOUSNESS (Islamic, Hindu, Confucian, Shinto) which had at least a chance of resisting or of transforming themselves into local competitors. An example is the MAJALLA, THE OTTOMAN CODIFICATION OF ISLAMIC HANAFI LAW OF OBLIGATIONS OF 1869–76, a serious peripheral attempt to adapt the European legal form of codification to Islamic substance. SOMETHING AT LEAST RESEMBLING 'CHOICE' WAS PROBABLY, ALONGSIDE 'IMPOSITION', A FACTOR IN CLT'S SUCCESS — in other words CLT probably had A CERTAIN INTRINSIC APPEAL for the elites that chose it. For CLT displaced an older Western transnational mode which asserted the existence of A UNIVERSAL LAW OF REASON (Catholic or natural-rights based) AND A SHARP LEGAL DISTINCTION BETWEEN CIVILISED (participants in ius gentium) AND BARBAROUS NATIONS. CLT offered the legal elites of the peripheral, newly created states of Europe, North and South America and Asia something at least superficially more attractive: THEY COULD IDENTIFY WITH THEIR OWN 'PEOPLES' AND SHARPLY DISSOCIATE THEMSELVES — being English, Russian, Argentinian, Egyptian or Japanese — FROM THE GERMANS AND THE FRENCH. They could deploy European historicist legal theory IN DEFENCE AGAINST EUROPEAN LEGAL HEGEMONY: only Latin American jurists could 'own' a Latin American law reflecting a CREOLE CONSCIOUSNESS, and Japanese law was to reflect the 'SPIRIT' of the Japanese people.

cards.q: What was the Majalla and what does it demonstrate?
cards.a: THE OTTOMAN CODIFICATION OF ISLAMIC HANAFI LAW OF OBLIGATIONS OF 1869–76 — a serious peripheral attempt to ADAPT THE EUROPEAN LEGAL FORM OF CODIFICATION TO ISLAMIC SUBSTANCE. It demonstrates that alongside 'imposition' 'CHOICE' played a part: CLT had a certain intrinsic appeal for the elites.

cards.q: What did CLT offer peripheral elites in place of the older Western mode?
cards.a: The older mode asserted A UNIVERSAL LAW OF REASON and A SHARP DISTINCTION BETWEEN CIVILISED AND BARBAROUS NATIONS. CLT allowed them to IDENTIFY WITH THEIR OWN 'PEOPLES' and sharply DISSOCIATE themselves from the Germans and the French — and TO DEPLOY EUROPEAN HISTORICIST THEORY IN DEFENCE AGAINST EUROPEAN LEGAL HEGEMONY (creole consciousness, the 'spirit' of the Japanese people).

13.title: The other side of the contradictory structure: ius gentium
13.text: On the other side of that contradictory structure, CLT asserted that EVERY COUNTRY WITH A WESTERN LEGAL HERITAGE SHARES THE ROMAN INHERITANCE ALONG WITH SAVIGNY'S GERMANS — INCLUDING, FOR INSTANCE, THE NEWLY INDEPENDENT BULGARIANS (1878/1908) AND BOLIVIANS (1825) — AND THAT EVERY NATION PARTICIPATING IN THE GLOBAL ORDER OF TRADE AND FINANCE PARTICIPATES IN THE IUS GENTIUM. Alongside the particularist notion that each people has its own unique normative order, jurists scattered across the periphery of independent nations and modernising empires could thus affirm their participation in the developing sciences of the law of obligations and of international law — founded on an analytics of will, right and sovereignty that HAD NO OBVIOUS NATIONAL PARTICULARITY. They could develop their own slightly modified national versions of the civil and commercial codes of the commercially, financially and militarily dominant European powers and thereby FACILITATE INTEGRATION INTO THE WORLD MARKET WITHOUT SEEING THEMSELVES AS TRAITORS TO THEIR NATIONAL CONSTITUENCIES. And they could work as jurists for their nations' interests within the structure of international law BY DEPLOYING THE NORMS OF SOVEREIGN EQUALITY AND AUTONOMY AGAINST THE GREAT POWERS. At home, the universal, transnational element in CLT was the basis of THEIR CLAIM TO POWER AS MEDIATORS OF THE PERIPHERY'S PARTICIPATION IN THE NORMATIVE ORDER AND THE CULTURE OF THE METROPOLES.

cards.q: How did CLT allow peripheral jurists to be nationalists and modernisers at once?
cards.a: Particularistically: each people has its own unique normative order. And UNIVERSALISTICALLY: every country with a Western heritage shares the ROMAN INHERITANCE and every nation in global trade participates in the IUS GENTIUM. They could thus develop modified versions of the European codes, FACILITATE INTEGRATION INTO THE WORLD MARKET AND NOT SEE THEMSELVES AS TRAITORS — while deploying the norms of SOVEREIGN EQUALITY against the great powers.

cards.q: What was the source of the peripheral jurists' power at home?
cards.a: THE UNIVERSAL, TRANSNATIONAL ELEMENT IN CLT — it was the basis of THEIR CLAIM TO POWER AS MEDIATORS OF THE PERIPHERY'S PARTICIPATION IN THE NORMATIVE ORDER AND THE CULTURE OF THE METROPOLES.

14.title: Three distinctions that eased the reception
14.text: Kennedy names THREE FURTHER STRUCTURAL FEATURES OF CLT that may have eased its acceptance first across Europe and then across the non-European periphery: (1) THE DISTINCTION BETWEEN THE 'SUBJECTS' OF DOMESTIC AND OF INTERNATIONAL LAW; (2) THE DISTINCTION BETWEEN PUBLIC AND PRIVATE LAW; (3) THE DISTINCTION BETWEEN THE LAW OF THE MARKET AND THE LAW OF THE HOUSEHOLD. AS TO THE FIRST: the subjects of domestic law include 'persons', but THE SUBJECTS OF INTERNATIONAL LAW IN CLT WERE ONLY 'SOVEREIGNS'. CITIZENS AS CITIZENS HAD NO RIGHTS UNDER INTERNATIONAL LAW — and if they had no rights, THEN SOVEREIGNS, AND ESPECIALLY POWERFUL SOVEREIGNS, HAD NO LEGAL BASIS FOR INTERFERING IN HOW INDEPENDENT STATES TREAT THEIR OWN CITIZENS. IT WAS A GLOBALIZATION OF A LEGAL CONSCIOUSNESS WHOSE BASIC STRUCTURAL FEATURE WAS THAT JURISDICTION MUST NOT BE GLOBAL. The recipients were legal elites scattered around the world, closely linked to the political and economic elites of their countries though not everywhere identical with them. ADOPTING CLT PERMITTED A GESTURE OF REMARKABLE COSMOPOLITANISM WITHOUT ANY SACRIFICE OF LOCAL AUTONOMY. AS TO THE SECOND: in CLT everyone understood — and jurists often asserted expressly — THAT PRIVATE LAW IS THE CORE OF LAW. That set apart not only international law but public law as well as NOT PART OF THE CORE. Public law (criminal, administrative, constitutional) was LESS SCIENTIFIC AND MORE POLITICAL: criminal law directly reflected the normative order of the common people; administrative law was the law of the sovereign, whose legal autonomy was in effect inherently unlimited; constitutional law was made by the people or the constituting orders of civil society as ultimate legal authors. THE CONSEQUENCE TO SEE: SCIENCE COMMITTED THE JURIST TO NOTHING WHATEVER ON THE QUESTION OF LOCAL DICTATORSHIP OR OLIGARCHIC RULE BY GREAT LANDOWNERS. At the same time public law was still, for all that, 'LAW', so the jurist could, if he cared to take the risk, deploy the prestige of Law in favour of one outcome or the other AT THE MOMENT OF A COUP — and he was certainly to be in charge of writing the new constitution when a new regime needed one.

cards.q: Who was the subject of international law in CLT, and what followed from that?
cards.a: ONLY SOVEREIGNS. Citizens as citizens had NO RIGHTS under international law — and hence SOVEREIGNS HAD NO LEGAL BASIS FOR INTERFERING IN HOW OTHER STATES TREAT THEIR CITIZENS. It was a consciousness whose basic feature was THAT JURISDICTION MUST NOT BE GLOBAL — and adopting CLT thus permitted A GESTURE OF COSMOPOLITANISM WITHOUT ANY SACRIFICE OF LOCAL AUTONOMY.

cards.q: Why was public law outside the core of CLT, and what followed politically?
cards.a: It was LESS SCIENTIFIC AND MORE POLITICAL: criminal law reflected the normative order of the common people, administrative law was the sovereign's law with inherently unlimited autonomy, constitutional law was made by the people as ultimate author. The consequence: SCIENCE COMMITTED THE JURIST TO NOTHING ON THE QUESTION OF LOCAL DICTATORSHIP OR OLIGARCHIC RULE BY GREAT LANDOWNERS.

15.title: Patriarchy: the will theory stops at the family
15.text: CLT dealt with the question of patriarchy — not merely of 'gender' but of the whole 'household' — by a distinction WITHIN PRIVATE LAW BETWEEN THE LAW OF OBLIGATIONS AND FAMILY LAW. And here is the formulation worth having verbatim: THE FIRST GLOBALIZATION GLOBALIZED A COMPROMISE IN WHICH THE WILL THEORY STOPPED AT THE FAMILY. There was a great difference between liberalism in the economy and liberalism in the relations of seducers and maidens, husbands and wives, fathers and abused or rebellious daughters, husbands and mistresses, former husbands and wives and their children, rich patriarchs and their proletarian boy lovers. The starting point was the 'EARLY MODERN' SYSTEM OF FAMILY LAW as described for instance by BLACKSTONE: THE PATRIARCH WAS LEGALLY BOUND TO SUPPORT HIS WIFE AND MINOR CHILDREN, WAS ENTITLED TO THEIR OBEDIENCE, WHICH HE COULD ENFORCE BY MODERATE CORPORAL PUNISHMENT, HAD DISCRETIONARY POWER over many aspects of their welfare and property AND WAS PROTECTED AGAINST SEXUAL AND ECONOMIC INTERFERENCE BY THIRD PARTIES. It was A LIMITED, CHRISTIANISED, SUPERVISED FORM OF PATRIARCHY, NOTHING LIKE THE ROMAN PATRIA POTESTAS: the father was understood to be subject to 'NATURAL' duties of care and protection going far beyond what market actors owe one another, and those were ENFORCEABLE against him in court, but ONLY AT THE OUTER LIMITS OF OUTRAGE. Within the wide space of discretion positive law gave him, JURISTS PRESENTED HIS HIGH ALTRUISTIC DUTIES AS MORAL OR ETHICAL RATHER THAN PROPERLY LEGAL — hence they were described as an 'IMPERFECT OBLIGATION' as against obligations 'perfected' by the addition of a state enforcement mechanism.

terms.def: The patriarch's high altruistic duties presented as moral rather than properly legal — as against obligations 'perfected' by state enforcement.

cards.q: How did CLT deal with patriarchy?
cards.a: By a distinction WITHIN PRIVATE LAW between the LAW OF OBLIGATIONS and FAMILY LAW: THE FIRST GLOBALIZATION GLOBALIZED A COMPROMISE IN WHICH THE WILL THEORY STOPPED AT THE FAMILY. There was a great difference between liberalism in the economy and liberalism in the relations within the household.

cards.q: Describe the early modern system of family law after Blackstone, and why it was not patria potestas.
cards.a: The patriarch was BOUND TO SUPPORT wife and minor children, was ENTITLED TO OBEDIENCE enforceable by MODERATE CORPORAL PUNISHMENT, had DISCRETIONARY POWER over much of their welfare and property, and was PROTECTED AGAINST INTERFERENCE BY THIRD PARTIES. It was not patria potestas because it was A LIMITED, CHRISTIANISED, SUPERVISED form: his 'natural' duties of care were ENFORCEABLE in court, but ONLY AT THE OUTER LIMITS OF OUTRAGE.

16.title: Family law around 1850 and formal equality without intervention
16.text: The North Atlantic regimes, when CLT started up around 1850, included some or all of the following: DIVORCE ONLY FOR FAULT OR NOT AT ALL, INHERITANCE RULES PROTECTING LEGITIMATE FAMILY ASSETS, THE CRIMINAL PROHIBITION OF 'UNNATURAL' AND 'DISHONOURABLE' SEXUALITY INCLUDING SAME-SEX SEX AND FEMALE ADULTERY (male adultery was usually punished only where linked with cohabitation or concubinage), THE SUPPRESSION OF LEGAL CLAIMS ARISING FROM 'IMMORAL' RELATIONS (especially the claims of mistresses and illegitimate children) AND THE AWARD OF CHILDREN TO THE FATHER. THE CODE NAPOLÉON (1804) was liberal in permitting DIVORCE BY MUTUAL CONSENT — THAT PROVISION WAS ABOLISHED IN 1815 UNDER THE RESTORATION AND RESTORED ONLY IN 1975. THE CHILEAN BELLO CODE OF 1857 took over much of the liberal law of obligations of the French code but HANDED THE WHOLE LAW OF MARRIAGE AND DIVORCE OVER TO THE CATHOLIC CHURCH TO ADMINISTER UNDER CANON LAW. Kennedy adds an observation that works well in an exam: IN 1850 THE FAMILY LAW OF THE NORTH ATLANTIC COUNTRIES STILL LOOKED, AT THE FORMAL LEVEL, RATHER LIKE THE MUSLIM, HINDU OR CONFUCIAN FAMILY LAW REGIMES OF THE TIME — and in some respects, such as Muslim marriage law, which recognised THE WIFE'S SEPARATE PROPERTY and treated DOMESTIC VIOLENCE and THE HUSBAND'S DUTY OF MAINTENANCE as fully justiciable, THE WEST WAS QUITE 'BEHIND' THE EAST. The substance of the North Atlantic regime then changed, historically speaking, rapidly towards FORMAL EQUALITY WITH RECIPROCAL DUTIES. In family relations this was formal equality within what the classics defined as 'STATUS', NOT CONTRACT, so that the terms of the parties' relation were determined by 'THE WILL OF THE STATE', NOT THE WILL OF THE PARTIES. CLT THUS SHARPLY SEPARATED FAMILY LAW FROM THE LAW OF OBLIGATIONS AND PLACED IT ON THE SIDE OF MORALS AND POLITICS, NOT SCIENCE AND WILL. And no less, perhaps more, importantly: CLT JOINED THE MOVE TOWARDS FORMAL EQUALITY WITH A POWERFUL DOCTRINE OF LEGAL NON-INTERVENTION IN THE FAMILY, WHICH MADE MUCH OF WIVES' FORMALLY EQUAL RIGHTS UNENFORCEABLE (domestic violence, marital rape). Non-intervention was justified on the ground that THE 'SPHERE' OF THE FAMILY, FOUNDED ON A PRINCIPLE OF EGALITARIAN ALTRUISM, WOULD BE CORRUPTED OR DESTROYED BY JUDICIAL INTERVENTION, WHICH WOULD HAVE TO USE LEGAL INSTRUMENTS CLOSELY BOUND UP WITH THE CONFLICTUAL INDIVIDUALIST ETHOS OF MARKET LAW.

cards.q: Was North Atlantic family law in 1850 more liberal than Muslim law?
cards.a: AT THE FORMAL LEVEL IT STILL LOOKED RATHER LIKE the Muslim, Hindu or Confucian regimes. And in some respects THE WEST WAS 'BEHIND': Muslim marriage law recognised THE WIFE'S SEPARATE PROPERTY and treated DOMESTIC VIOLENCE and THE HUSBAND'S DUTY OF MAINTENANCE as fully justiciable.

cards.q: Where did CLT place family law, and what did it add to formal equality?
cards.a: It SHARPLY SEPARATED it from the law of obligations and placed it ON THE SIDE OF MORALS AND POLITICS, NOT SCIENCE AND WILL — it was formal equality within 'STATUS', not contract, so the terms were set by 'the will of the state'. And it joined it with A POWERFUL DOCTRINE OF LEGAL NON-INTERVENTION IN THE FAMILY, which made much of wives' formally equal rights UNENFORCEABLE.

cards.q: How was non-intervention in the family justified?
cards.a: That THE 'SPHERE' OF THE FAMILY, FOUNDED ON A PRINCIPLE OF EGALITARIAN ALTRUISM, WOULD BE CORRUPTED OR DESTROYED BY JUDICIAL INTERVENTION, because intervention would have to use LEGAL INSTRUMENTS CLOSELY BOUND UP WITH THE CONFLICTUAL INDIVIDUALIST ETHOS OF MARKET LAW.

17.title: The colonies: 'indigenous' family law was left alone
17.text: THE COLONIAL POWERS EVERYWHERE REFUSED TO REPLACE 'INDIGENOUS' FAMILY LAW WITH THEIR OWN SYSTEMS. EVEN THE FRENCH, famous for 'direct rule' and 'assimilation', did no more than support THE CODIFICATION OF MUSLIM FAMILY LAW in the Maghreb. THE BRITISH did the same in India, WITH SEPARATE HINDU, MUSLIM AND CHRISTIAN RULES. In the DUTCH EAST INDIES the Dutch preserved ADAT LAW for the family. But everywhere the process of formalisation within the colonial legal and political system involved SOME DELIBERATE CHANGE (for example in practices such as widow-burning in India) and set off MANY INDIRECT CHANGES, INTENDED AND UNINTENDED — and these could STRENGTHEN RATHER THAN WEAKEN THE POWER OF HOUSEHOLD HEADS by reducing the accountability of titular landholders to members of the extended family. There appear to have been very many solutions, along a highly predictable continuum of possibilities, and the outcome in many countries was determined by SHARP CONFLICTS BETWEEN THE CATHOLIC CHURCH, SOCIALLY CONSERVATIVE PROTESTANT SECTS OR MUSLIM CLERICS ON ONE SIDE AND 'MODERNISING' SECULAR FORCES ON THE OTHER. Although the continuum of solutions and the arguments back and forth were apparently the same everywhere, THE SOLUTIONS ADOPTED IN NORTH AMERICA WERE MUCH MORE 'LIBERAL' THAN THOSE IN SOUTH AMERICA AND IN THE FORMER OTTOMAN EMPIRE; IN EUROPE THERE WERE AS MANY COMPROMISES AS THERE WERE COUNTRIES, and everywhere they were unstable, with change generally in a liberalising direction interrupted by periods of reaction.

cards.q: How did the colonial powers deal with 'indigenous' family law?
cards.a: THEY EVERYWHERE REFUSED TO REPLACE IT with their own systems. The French in the Maghreb merely supported THE CODIFICATION OF MUSLIM family law, the British in India did the same with SEPARATE HINDU, MUSLIM AND CHRISTIAN rules, and the Dutch in the East Indies preserved ADAT law.

cards.q: What unintended effect could the colonial formalisation of family law have?
cards.a: It could STRENGTHEN RATHER THAN WEAKEN THE POWER OF HOUSEHOLD HEADS — by REDUCING THE ACCOUNTABILITY OF TITULAR LANDHOLDERS TO MEMBERS OF THE EXTENDED FAMILY.

18.title: The Savignyan bargain: a national family for a universal market
18.text: Kennedy's key hypothesis about why it worked. The distinction between MARKET AND FAMILY LAW functioned in the context of historicism just as the domestic/international and public/private distinctions did. CLT DID NOT CLAIM SUBSTANTIVE UNIVERSALITY — QUITE THE CONTRARY. BEGINNING WITH SAVIGNY IT OFFERED PERIPHERAL ELITES THE CATEGORISATION OF THEIR FAMILY LAW AS POPULAR, POLITICAL, RELIGIOUS, CULTURAL AND PARTICULAR, AND THEREFORE EMINENTLY NATIONAL. IN EXCHANGE THEY ACCEPTED — USUALLY EAGERLY — THAT THE LAW OF THE MARKET WOULD BE, NOT POSITIVELY AND IN EVERY DETAIL BUT GENERALLY AND 'IN ESSENCE', THE LAW OF A NATIONAL 'FREE' MARKET FOUNDED ON PROPERTY AND CONTRACT, LINKED TO THE OTHER FREE MARKETS BY FREE TRADE, THE GOLD STANDARD AND A PRIVATE INTERNATIONAL LAW CONCEPTUALLY IDENTICAL WITH DOMESTIC CIVIL LAW. In the first half of the 19th century, however, another boundary question had first to be settled BEFORE THE CONSCIOUSNESS OF THE FIRST GLOBALIZATION COULD SOLIDIFY — and it did not concern the blood family. For the blood family, the solution that full liberalisation does not apply and that each country may make its own compromise between equality and tradition was A STABLE OVERARCHING CONTEXT FOR LOCAL BATTLES. The harder question was THE STATUS OF WHAT THE 18TH CENTURY UNDERSTOOD AS DOMESTIC LABOUR: THE LABOUR OF SLAVES, APPRENTICES, INDENTURED SERVANTS AND DEPENDENT AGRICULTURAL WORKERS.

cards.q: Describe the 'Savignyan bargain' between CLT and the peripheral elites.
cards.a: CLT offered the elites the categorisation of their FAMILY LAW as POPULAR, POLITICAL, RELIGIOUS, CULTURAL AND PARTICULAR, THEREFORE EMINENTLY NATIONAL. IN EXCHANGE THEY ACCEPTED that THE LAW OF THE MARKET would generally and 'in essence' be THE LAW OF A NATIONAL 'FREE' MARKET founded on PROPERTY AND CONTRACT, linked to the other markets by FREE TRADE, THE GOLD STANDARD AND PRIVATE INTERNATIONAL LAW.

19.title: Self-ownership and the end of the household
19.text: In the North Atlantic the final solution came WITH THE RISE OF THE FACTORY, THE SMALL FARM AND THE BOURGEOIS (as opposed to aristocratic) INSTITUTION OF DOMESTIC SERVICE as the dominant forms of labour. ALL THOSE CLASSES OF LABOUR WERE, IN THE LIBERAL REGIME OF CLT'S WILL THEORY AND FREE CONTRACT, BROUGHT UNDER THE CONCEPT OF 'SELF-OWNERSHIP' INSTEAD OF THE 18TH-CENTURY MODEL IN WHICH THE SERVANT IS PART OF THE HOUSEHOLD. THE DUTIES OF OBEDIENCE WERE REMOVED ALONG WITH THE RIGHTS TO MAINTENANCE; THE DISCRETIONARY AUTHORITY OF THE EMPLOYER REPLACED THE DISCRETIONARY AUTHORITY OF THE PATRIARCH. THE INTERMEDIATE FORMS OF SEMI-FREE LABOUR — SERFDOM, APPRENTICESHIP, INDENTURE — DISAPPEARED: through the French Revolution and Napoleon's conquests in western Europe, at the moment of independence from Spain in Latin America, after mid-century in Russia. SLAVERY FLOURISHED THROUGH THE 19TH CENTURY IN MANY COUNTRIES OF THE AMERICAS AND WAS ABOLISHED IN THE USA ONLY IN 1863, IN BRAZIL IN 1871 AND FINALLY IN CUBA IN 1886. AT THAT MOMENT ALL THAT REMAINED OF THE LEGAL HOUSEHOLD WAS THE FAMILY.

terms.def: The concept under which CLT brought all forms of labour, in place of the model of the servant as part of the household — duties of obedience disappeared along with rights to maintenance.

cards.q: What did CLT do with the forms of labour, and what was exchanged thereby?
cards.a: It brought them all under the concept of 'SELF-OWNERSHIP' in place of the 18th-century model of the servant as part of the household. THE DUTIES OF OBEDIENCE WERE REMOVED ALONG WITH THE RIGHTS TO MAINTENANCE, and THE DISCRETIONARY AUTHORITY OF THE EMPLOYER REPLACED THAT OF THE PATRIARCH.

cards.q: When was slavery abolished in the Americas, and what remained of the household?
cards.a: In the USA only IN 1863, IN BRAZIL IN 1871 and finally IN CUBA IN 1886. The intermediate forms of semi-free labour (serfdom, apprenticeship, indenture) had disappeared earlier — through the Revolution and Napoleon in western Europe, with independence in Latin America, after mid-century in Russia. AT THAT MOMENT ALL THAT REMAINED OF THE LEGAL HOUSEHOLD WAS THE FAMILY.

20.title: Latifundia and minifundia: why CLT could be globalized
20.text: In the global South, that is on the capitalist periphery broadly conceived, THE SMALL FARM SO CENTRAL TO NORTH ATLANTIC REPUBLICAN IDEOLOGY DID NOT EMERGE. European diseases and extermination removed most of the remaining hunter-gatherers and nomadic pastoralists and merged tribal societies and small states into colonies; at the same time the pre-capitalist empires broke up into nation states or colonies. WITHIN THAT STRUCTURE A VERY LARGE PART OF THE WORLD'S POPULATION CAME TO BE ORGANISED EITHER IN 'LATIFUNDIA' — GREAT ESTATES OR PLANTATIONS, OWNED FIRST BY PLANTERS AND THEN BY TRANSNATIONAL FIRMS, WORKED BY NOMINALLY FREE BUT IN FACT DEPENDENT LABOURERS — OR IN 'MINIFUNDIA', SMALL PLOTS WORKED BY PEASANT VILLAGERS UNDER VARIOUS FORMS OF CUSTOMARY OR SHARECROPPING TENURE. Both types produced old or new cash crops for the new world market, the smallholders in an unstable combination with subsistence crops. The latifundia/minifundia contrast holds for Latin America, Africa, India, eastern Europe, the successor states of the Ottoman Empire, Indonesia, China and the post-war American South alike. The incorporation of those labour forms into the categories of CLT — THE SALE OF LABOUR POWER for the agricultural worker, PRIVATE OWNERSHIP OF LAND for the peasant — sometimes meant that colonial powers and independent peripheral states SIMPLY RATIFIED, BY ADOPTING A FORMAL, ABSTRACT CONCEPTION OF FREE WILL RATHER THAN A MORE SUBSTANTIVE ONE, WHATEVER SCHEMES OF ECONOMIC AND SOCIAL HIERARCHY HAD EMERGED ON THE GROUND FROM THE PLAY OF VIOLENCE AND CULTURE. And sometimes they TRANSFORMED them, in their own interest but without a precise understanding of what they were doing, BY FORCING PRE-EXISTING SOCIAL ARRANGEMENTS INTO THE FORM OF 'THE WESTERN IDEA OF PROPERTY'. Throughout the long transition a whole range of LEGAL CONTORTIONS was available, so that something like serfdom could be maintained within liberal forms and something like capitalism within feudal ones. (The great exception is BRITISH INDIA, where LAND REFORM was from the mid-19th century A PRINCIPAL STRATEGY OF CONTROL and of colonial reconstitution.) AND HERE IS THE POINT: IT SEEMS PLAUSIBLE THAT CLT COULD BE GLOBALIZED PRECISELY BECAUSE IT HAD SO LITTLE TO SAY ONE WAY OR THE OTHER ABOUT THE LEGAL TREATMENT OF THE LEGALLY FREE BUT OBVIOUSLY SUBORDINATED PEASANTS AND AGRICULTURAL WORKERS OF THE SOUTH.

terms.def: Great estates worked by nominally free but in fact dependent labourers vs small plots worked by peasant villagers under customary or sharecropping tenure.

cards.q: What are latifundia and minifundia, and where does that contrast hold?
cards.a: LATIFUNDIA = great estates or plantations owned by planters and then by transnational firms, worked by NOMINALLY FREE BUT IN FACT DEPENDENT labourers. MINIFUNDIA = small plots worked by peasant villagers under customary or SHARECROPPING tenure. It holds for Latin America, Africa, India, eastern Europe, the Ottoman successor states, Indonesia, China and the post-war American South.

cards.q: Why, on Kennedy's account, could CLT be globalized at all?
cards.a: PRECISELY BECAUSE IT HAD SO LITTLE TO SAY ONE WAY OR THE OTHER ABOUT THE LEGAL TREATMENT OF THE LEGALLY FREE BUT OBVIOUSLY SUBORDINATED PEASANTS AND AGRICULTURAL WORKERS OF THE SOUTH. By adopting a FORMAL, ABSTRACT conception of free will it merely RATIFIED the hierarchies that had emerged on the ground from the play of violence and culture.
